one_month_reasoning: No Oracle earnings in the window (Q2 FY27 is due mid-December). Scheduled: Oracle AI World Oct 25-28 (product/customer news, sometimes analyst commentary; usually mildly positive), and the Big-4 Q3 calls around Oct 28-30, which bring the first numeric 2027 capex guides. Per the standing capex view those are more likely up than down and help the AI-infrastructure narrative, but ORCL now trades on its own credit/financing risk (record CDS, force majeure at Project Jupiter, Wisconsin power delay). Unscheduled: OpenAI's ~$30B raise at ~$1.4T (Bloomberg 9/29) closing would be a positive counterparty signal, and further site-delay or rating news a negative one. These roughly offset, so I stay close to a symmetric lognormal around $143.41 at ~16% monthly vol (56%/3.5), with no drift and only the usual lognormal skew.

fair_value.method: Fair value 12 months out (Oct-2027): 60% P/E (NTM EPS then ~$11.1 x 15x = $166) and 40% EV/EBITDA (NTM EBITDA ~$58B x 11.5x = $667B EV, less ~$157B net debt, over 3.12B shares = $164). Both multiples sit in the lower half of a 10-11 company peer set because of leverage, negative FCF and OpenAI concentration.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 = 0.6 x FY28 $10.3 + 0.4 x FY29 $12.3 = ~$11.1; multiple 15x (peer CY2027 median 22.5x, range 8.5-27.0x)

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus is $11.00 (Yahoo, 39 analysts, range 9.00-13.30), but another aggregate cited on 9/30 is $9.13. I take ~$10.3 (about 6% under Yahoo) for Wisconsin/Jupiter power delays, ~5% dilution from the $20B ATM plus the mandatory convertible, and rising interest cost.

FY28 consensus growth is +35%; ~half of the $664B RPO converts within 36 months, and the CY2028 Oracle capex base is $130B. I assume growth slows to ~+19% because margins dilute and depreciation ramps.

Peer CY2027 median is 22.5x (range 8.5-27.0x). I place ORCL with IBM 16.8x, CRM 14.3x and WDAY 14.2x, a ~33% discount to the median, despite +35% FY28 EPS growth: net debt ~$132B, TTM FCF -$23.7B, CDS ~200-222bp (4x IG), BBB- one notch from junk, and ~half of RPO from one unprofitable customer. These are balance-sheet and concentration features that persist through the horizon (capex guided $90-95B for FY27 and rising in CY2028).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Oct-2027 ~$135B x 43% EBITDA margin = ~$58B; x 11.5x = $667B EV; net debt ~$157B; 3.12B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.6 x FY28 ~$125B (consensus $131.7B less ~$7B for power-delayed capacity at Wisconsin/Jupiter) + 0.4 x FY29 ~$150B.

TTM EBITDA $34.4B on ~$71.8B TTM revenue (FY26 $67.4B + Q1 y/y increase of $4.4B) is ~48%. Management flags a further gross-margin step-down as lower-margin AI infrastructure grows, so I take ~5pt off.

Peer TTM EV/EBITDA median is 17.7x (range 9.4-49.5x). A forward multiple runs ~15-20% lower for growing peers. I apply a further discount for capital intensity and leverage, between ADBE 9.4x and IBM 16.2x TTM. ORCL today trades at 16.5x TTM.
$132B today (stockanalysis, incl. leases; debt $125.3B less cash $37.1B = $88B ex-leases) plus ~$25B: FY27 net capex <= $70B against OCF, partly funded by prepayments and equity.
3,024M outstanding at 8/31/26 after the $19.9B ATM in Q1, plus ~3% for the mandatory convertible and further issuance.

bear.story: Financing and counterparty stress. OpenAI's raise stalls or it re-scopes Stargate commitments, and power delays (Jupiter force majeure, Wisconsin PSC refiling) push $20B+ of revenue past FY28. A downgrade to high yield forces more dilutive equity. FY28 EPS ~$8.5 at ~10x CY2028 EPS less leverage drag, or ~7-8x EBITDA.

base.story: Capacity keeps landing (850 MW in Q1, Abilene 75% delivered, Shackelford 1H27), and FY28 EPS comes in at ~$10-10.5, a bit under consensus. Credit spreads stay wide but stable, and the stock re-rates only partly, to ~14-15x NTM EPS, as FCF turns less negative on prepayments and BYO hardware.

bull.story: OpenAI closes ~$30B at ~$1.4T and moves toward a 2027 IPO (Kalshi ~75% announce by Jun-27), which removes the counterparty overhang. GPU rental prices stay firm (B200 +79% in 3 months), RPO conversion accelerates, CDS tightens and the multiple goes back to ~20x on ~$12 NTM EPS.

comps_summary.peer_range: P/E on calendar-2027 street EPS (fiscal years converted to calendar): 8.5x (ADBE) to 27.0x (NOW), median 22.5x across 10 profitable peers. EV/EBITDA is TTM from stockanalysis, because forward EBITDA was not accessible: 9.4x (ADBE) to 49.5x (NOW), median 17.7x across 11.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: ORCL is at 14.6x CY2027 consensus EPS ($9.81 = 5/12 x 8.14 + 7/12 x 11.00) and 16.5x TTM EV/EBITDA. I use 15x NTM P/E and 11.5x forward EV/EBITDA at the horizon, in the lower third of the range and about a third below the median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: I give no premium for ORCL's faster EPS growth (+35% FY28 consensus vs ~10-20% for peers) because that growth is bought with leverage and concentration that persist through the horizon. Net debt is ~$132B, TTM FCF is -$23.7B, and gross capex is guided at $90-95B for FY27 with more in CY2028. CDS is at a record 200-222bp and the rating is one notch above junk. About half of the $664B RPO is tied to OpenAI. The AI rental mix is diluting margins, and the stock needs ongoing equity issuance ($19.9B ATM in one quarter). The closest business-model comp, CoreWeave, is loss-making. The discount puts ORCL with IBM/CRM/WDAY rather than the hyperscaler cluster at 22-24x.

thesis_break_reason: $95 is ~17% below the $114.50 52-week low. At that price the market cap (~$290B) is barely 2x net debt and EV/NTM EBITDA is ~7x. That would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than volatility: OpenAI re-scoping or deferring its Oracle commitment, a downgrade to high yield that forces deeply dilutive equity, or multi-site power delays (Jupiter, Wisconsin) that push FY28 revenue well below ~$115B.

reasoning: Reported facts (Q1 FY27, 9/10): revenue +30% to $19.3B, OCI +121% to $7.4B, non-GAAP EPS $1.92, RPO $664B (+$26B q/q, ~13% within 12 months, ~half within 36), capex $28.5B gross / ~$18B net, TTM FCF -$23.7B, debt $125B, and $19.9B of ATM equity in one quarter (shares 2.88B to 3.02B). The FY27 capex guide is $90-95B gross and at most $70B net. I convert estimates to a calendar basis: CY2027 EPS = 5/12 x 8.14 + 7/12 x 11.00 = $9.81, so the stock is at 14.6x against a 10-peer CY2027 median of 22.5x. Another aggregate puts FY28 at $9.13, so I haircut to ~$10.3. Alternative-lane evidence is mixed. Negative: Aterio site data says the 1.3 GW Wisconsin campus likely misses 2H27 (PSC case refiled 9/18). Oracle invoked force majeure on Project Jupiter (9/24). CDS hit a record ~222bp, one notch above junk (Barchart via X, confirmed by press). Critics (Zitron newsletter/X, a Substack on circular financing) frame OpenAI as an existential counterparty risk, and Reddit attention spiked on the force-majeure news. Positive: GPU rental trackers show B200 prices up ~79% in three months (shattered.io, Mercatus, GPUPerHour), so AI compute demand is not slackening. OpenAI is raising ~$30B at ~$1.4T (Bloomberg 9/29). Prediction markets give an OpenAI IPO announcement ~75% by Jun-2027 (Kalshi), though Polymarket's 2027 legs are thin (46% by Jun-30-2027). Job-posting data show OCI software roles cut but DC/GPU ops roles kept. Fair value of ~$165 blends P/E (15x on ~$11.1 NTM EPS at Oct-27) with EV/EBITDA (11.5x). Scenarios are bear $82 (27%), base $152 (48%) and bull $240 (25%), each a lognormal with 22-30% dispersion. The mixture has a median ~$150 and a mean ~$155. Implied annual vol is ~50%, close to the 56% realized and above the ±25-35% typical for large caps, because the outcome is binary-ish on OpenAI and financing. P(>=143) = 0.55. Research was limited: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data estimates were paywalled, so peer EPS came from Yahoo analysis pages and EV/EBITDA is TTM. About 54% of sources are in-lane; the out-of-lane ones are mostly filings and consensus data needed for the valuation.
